source: Task 9 (cross-language digest fixtures) -- see fixtures/distributions/univariate/mixture.json for the primary Mixture coverage; this file exists only to pin a second, larger seeded draw stream shared verbatim by all four runners.
reference: Not a C# unit test transcription -- expected values are curated via `tools/oracle_emitter --dump` against the real Numerics Mixture.GenerateRandomValues and reproduced by tools/verify_oracles.py, per fixtures/README.md's curation path.
note: A two-component Normal mixture (distinct from the three-component construct mixture.json's own seeded_sampling case uses), n = 20 draws seeded at 12345 -- both the component count and the seed are new coverage, not a repeat of the existing seed-42/n-5 pin. The point of this fixture is the CROSS-LANGUAGE guarantee: the same three pinned draws (first, middle, last of the stream) are asserted by the C++, R and Python runners off the identical JSON literal, so R and Python agreeing is proven by both independently reproducing the real C# Mersenne-Twister/component-selection stream rather than by a separate comparison step.
